name: Namhansanseong
description: Namhansanseong is a mountaintop fortress city about 25 km south-east of Seoul, where its walls run roughly 12 km along the ridges of Namhansan. Built as a refuge for Joseon kings, it was defended by Buddhist monk-soldiers and could shelter around 4,000 people. Its layered walls show how fortress design shifted with the arrival of gunpowder weapons, and it remains a lasting symbol of Korean sovereignty.
